compatibility.title: Which Kia and Hyundai Models Use the D4HA?
compatibility.intro: The D4HA is the 2.0‑litre member of Hyundai‑Kia's R‑family diesel engines, fitted primarily to large SUVs and executive models. It powers the Kia Sorento and Hyundai Santa Fe across two generations, with power outputs ranging from 138 hp to 184 hp depending on tuning.
compatibility.closing: Not sure which engine your car has? Enter your registration above - we'll confirm your exact D4HA fitment before any quotes are sent.

costGuide.title: Kia D4HA Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a D4HA typically takes 8-11 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent specialist) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: The D4HA is a well‑supported engine with strong parts availability. Prices vary based on whether the timing chain has been done, whether injectors have been refurbished, and whether the engine is from a 138 hp or 184 hp tune. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for context.

failures.title: Kia D4HA Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing chain stretch
items.whatHappens: The D4HA's timing chain can stretch over time, leading to poor starting, rough running and, in severe cases, camshaft timing errors. This is a well‑documented issue across the R‑family diesel engines. Symptoms include a rattling noise on cold start, check engine light with timing‑related codes, and reduced performance.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing chain replacement (around £800-£1,500 at an independent specialist) is the standard fix. This is far cheaper than a full engine replacement and should be considered preventative maintenance on higher‑mileage engines. If the chain has jumped, valve damage may require a full rebuild. Read our full timing chain failure guide

items.title: Injector failure
items.whatHappens: The common‑rail injectors on the D4HA can fail, leading to rough idle, poor performance, excessive smoke, and increased fuel consumption. Injector seal leaks are also common on high‑mileage examples.
items.repairVsReplace: Injectors can be refurbished (around £150-£300 each) or replaced (around £300-£500 each). This is a routine repair on high‑mileage diesels and not a reason for engine replacement.

items.title: DPF clogging
items.whatHappens: Like all modern diesels, the D4HA is susceptible to DPF clogging, particularly on vehicles used predominantly for short urban journeys. Symptoms include reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and the DPF warning light.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning (around £300-£500) is usually sufficient. If the DPF is damaged, replacement costs around £800-£1,200. This is a maintenance issue, not a reason to replace the engine.

items.title: EGR valve and cooler issues
items.whatHappens: EGR valve clogging and EGR cooler failures are common on high‑mileage D4HA engines. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation, and potentially the engine entering limp mode.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR valve cleaning (around £200-£400) is usually sufficient; EGR cooler replacement costs around £500-£800 if it is leaking.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the D4HA
variants.intro: The D4HA is a specific engine code within the Hyundai‑Kia R‑family of diesel engines. Unlike some engine families that fragment into many sub‑codes, the D4HA variants are primarily distinguished by power output and application. R‑Family Overview: The R‑family includes: - D4EA - 2.0L CRDi, predecessor to D4HA, fitted to earlier Santa Fe and Sorento models - D4HA - 2.0L CRDi, the main 2.0‑litre R‑family variant, 138-184 hp - D4FB - 1.6L CRDi, fitted to i30, Cee'd and Sportage - D4FD - 1.7L CRDi, fitted to i40 and Sportage - D4FE - 2.0L CRDi, Smartstream successor to D4HA Within the D4HA, the key distinctions are: - 138 hp (101 kW) variant - lower‑output tune, fitted to entry‑level Sorento and Santa Fe - 150 hp (110 kW) variant - mid‑range tune - 184 hp (135 kW) variant - high‑output tune, fitted to top‑spec Sorento and Santa Fe models - Turbocharger differences - high‑output variants use a variable geometry turbo (VGT) compared to the simpler fixed‑geometry turbo on lower‑output versions How to confirm your code: 1. On the engine - the D4HA code is stamped on the engine block. Look for "D4HA" on the identification plate on the left‑hand side of the engine. 2. On the V5C logbook - the engine number is listed; cross‑reference with Hyundai‑Kia parts systems. 3. VIN decode - use a Hyundai‑Kia VIN decoder; the engine type will be shown. 4. Registration lookup - enter your reg above and we'll confirm the exact fitment. Similar‑looking codes it is commonly confused with: - Kia D4FB 1.6 CRDi - the 1.6‑litre R‑family variant, fitted to Cee'd and Sportage; different displacement and power - Kia D4FD 1.7 CRDi - the 1.7‑litre R‑family variant, fitted to i40 and Sportage - Hyundai D4FE 2.0 Smartstream - the successor to D4HA, fitted to newer Santa Fe and Sorento models

relatives.description: D4EA: - the 2.0-litre CRDi that preceded the D4HA in earlier Sorento and Santa Fe models. It used a simpler common-rail system and lower injection pressures, producing 138-148 hp. The D4HA brought higher injection pressure and improved emissions compliance.

variants.closing: Why fitting the wrong revision matters: The D4HA's turbocharger, injectors and ECU calibration differ between the 138 hp, 150 hp and 184 hp variants. A high‑output 184 hp engine will work in a lower‑output application with appropriate ECU programming, but a lower‑output engine fitted to a high‑output vehicle will feel underpowered and may have compatibility issues with the vehicle's engine management.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement D4HA - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used D4HA makes sense for lower‑value Sorento or Santa Fe examples where the car itself is worth under £3,000-£4,000. The key requirement is documented service history with the correct oil specification, and evidence that the timing chain and injectors have been addressed if over 100,000 miles. The primary risk with used units is undisclosed chain stretch or injector wear - insist on a cold start noise check, injector balance test and compression check before purchase. Used units typically cost £500-£1,200. View used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper D4HA recon includes new timing chain kit, refurbished or new injectors, new DPF (or professional clean), new EGR valve, and full gasket set. This is the right call for most replacements - you get a like‑new unit with the known weak points already addressed, backed by 12-24 months warranty. Reconditioned units typically cost £1,500-£2,800. View reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified for high‑value examples or where the existing engine has suffered catastrophic failure (e.g. chain jumped and bent valves). An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons, rings, bearings, and a full set of gaskets. For standard applications, reconditioned is usually more cost‑effective. View rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Kia and Hyundai specialists - nationwide coverage with 12‑month warranty on labour and parts. View supply & fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The D4HA sits in large SUVs - Kia Sorento (£3,000-£10,000), Hyundai Santa Fe (£3,000-£12,000). A £1,500-£2,800 reconditioned engine plus £700-£1,000 fitting is a significant but often justifiable investment - typically 20-40% of the vehicle's value. For lower‑value examples (sub‑£4,000 Sorento or Santa Fe), a used engine with documented timing chain and injector history may be more economic. For well‑maintained, high‑spec examples, the investment is usually justified given the vehicle's remaining life and capability. Always evaluate the whole‑vehicle condition before committing.

items.question: What are the common problems with the Kia D4HA engine?
items.answer: The D4HA's most common issues are timing chain stretch (80,000-150,000 miles), injector failure, DPF clogging (urban driving), and EGR valve/cooler issues. The engine is generally reliable when maintained properly. Timing chain stretch is the most critical issue. Injector failure causes rough running and excessive smoke. DPF cleaning is standard maintenance for urban vehicles.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned D4HA engine?
items.answer: A used D4HA makes sense only with documented service history and evidence of timing chain work if over 100,000 miles. A reconditioned unit is safer, including new chain kit, injectors and EGR valve with 12-24 months warranty, typically costing £1,500-£2,800 supply-only. Used engines risk undisclosed chain stretch and injector issues. Cold start noise test and injector balance check are essential. Reconditioned units address known failure points.

items.question: How do I know if my Kia or Hyundai has the D4HA engine?
items.answer: The D4HA is stamped on the engine block - look for "D4HA" on the identification plate on the left-hand side of the engine. You can also decode your VIN using Hyundai-Kia parts systems. Enter your registration above for confirmation. The V5C logbook lists the engine number. Hyundai-Kia VIN decoders show engine type as "D4HA". Power output (138 hp, 150 hp or 184 hp) indicates the variant.

items.question: Is the D4HA a reliable engine?
items.answer: Yes - the D4HA is generally considered a reliable engine when properly maintained. With regular oil changes using the correct specification, D4HA engines regularly exceed 200,000 miles. The R-family is one of Hyundai-Kia's most successful diesel platforms. Timing chain maintenance is the key to longevity. Regular oil changes using the correct spec are essential. DPF regeneration requires motorway driving for urban vehicles.
